record.name: Storage
record.purpose: The standards this group works to.

says: Alice founds a Team alone on her laptop and then changes her own grant in it eight times, each change expecting the Team head the previous one moved to, while the process is killed at a different durable boundary of each control commit — before staging, after the member write before sync, after staging before rename, after rename before the directory sync, after that sync before the transaction begins, inside the transaction before commit, after commit before the answer returns, and during the checkpoint that follows — and restarted. Each request is then answered once, committed, and the next change is accepted on the head it expects, so no control was applied twice or left half applied. The change killed inside its transaction, whose answer the caller never saw, is settled by querying its request id: the original result and its receipt. The same request id with other bytes (another grant) is refused with request_id_conflict; a change still expecting a Team head that has since advanced is refused as stale with stale_base; a cancellation of the last committed change reaches the owner after its commit and is refused with cancel_too_late; and querying that change afterwards still returns its committed result and receipt. What must not happen: a duplicate or second grant revision from one request, a refused request moving the Team head, or the late cancellation undoing the commit.
